title: Dielectric and dielectric constant
notes: A dielectric is an insulating material. Its molecules polarise in an electric field, so a thin layer of bound charge appears on the surfaces.

The dielectric constant K, also called the relative permittivity, is the factor by which the capacitance of a vacuum capacitor increases when the dielectric fills it: C = K C_0. For vacuum, K = 1. For water and many insulators, K is greater than 1.
With the charge on the plates held fixed, the polarisation opposes the field, so the net field and the potential difference fall. Since C = Q/V, a smaller V means a larger C.
The force between two charges in a uniform medium is the vacuum force divided by K. The medium does not remove the charges. It reduces the force.
A dielectric lets the capacitor be used at a higher voltage before sparking, up to the dielectric strength. That is a separate limit from the value of K.
If the capacitor stays connected to a battery, V is fixed and inserting the dielectric increases Q. If it is disconnected, Q is fixed and V falls. The two experiments are different.

exercises.question: A vacuum capacitor has C_0 = 2.0 μF. A dielectric of K = 4 fills it. The capacitor is isolated with charge fixed. Find the new capacitance and say what happens to the potential difference.
steps: Q is fixed because the capacitor is isolated.
V = Q/C, and C has increased, so V falls to one quarter.
The field inside falls for the same reason.
If the battery had stayed connected, V would have stayed the same and Q would have risen.
exercises.answer: 8.0 μF, and the potential difference falls to one quarter.
